title: The wall-stack holdout reduced to integers: no count fails, no halt
text: For 1RB1LF_1LC1RD_1RA1LA_0RA0RE_0RC---_1RF0LC, Lean now proves that the rules on the tape cover the integer counter-stack model on every wall, so the machine never halts if the integer recursion from its step start never makes a count fail. The kernel checks the first 50,000 steps of that recursion, and Python runs it for 3,000,000 steps (no halt in the first 10<sup>528,274</sup> steps). The bound 'each counter at least 5 times the one below', seen along the whole orbit, is not kept by the rules: a wall that satisfies it fails after 16 odd signals. What is left is a 2-adic avoidance statement on pairs of counters.
